title: 01 / The problem
caption: A read-only workflow helps maintainers collect evidence, find related reports and prepare a reply without guessing the cause.

title: 02 / A complete tool plugin
caption: The Dify SDK plugin exposes two read-only tools. A token is optional for public API access and is configured as a provider secret.

title: 03 / Bounded API access
caption: Repository syntax is validated before an API call. Requests use a fixed HTTPS host and explicit timeouts, with distinct actionable error codes.

title: 04 / Workflow variables
caption: The tool adapter returns status and payload_json as explicit SDK variables. The Workflow parses the payload and routes expected errors instead of inventing a diagnosis.

title: 05 / Complete live execution
caption: Now the published Web App runs the entire Workflow against a real public GitHub issue. Captured screens show the real input, execution and result; this walkthrough is edited for presentation.

title: 06 / Inspect the real trace
caption: The Studio trace shows seven successful nodes in 2.759 seconds, with zero model tokens. Both API tools and the processing and conditional nodes executed.

title: 07 / Review the evidence
caption: The result identifies the source issue, reports a rule-based connectivity signal and proposes an investigation order. These are triage signals, not a confirmed root cause.

title: 08 / Candidates and a draft reply
caption: Related reports are keyword candidates only. The reply remains a draft for review, and the workflow never posts it or changes the issue.

title: 09 / Invalid input
caption: An invalid repository is handled by the stop branch. The result explains the required input format and explicitly says that no diagnosis was generated.

title: 10 / Limits and submission
caption: The source, exported DSL and tested Web App are available. This captioned recording template has no candidate narration; add your own spoken English explanation before submitting it as the candidate walkthrough.
